archetypes.name: scout-sidecar-pipeline
archetypes.rationale: The scout sidecar is a new multi-stage pipeline (Python parser → shell filter → materialization) with several subtle correctness risks that are distinct from what static reviewers cover.
archetypes.prompt_body: Focus on `scripts/parse-drafter-output.py`: the `plan_contains_standalone_scout_manifest` function sets `unfenced_text = plan_text if in_fence else '\n'.join(unfenced_lines)` — when a fence is never closed, it uses the raw plan_text and scans fenced examples as unfenced, potentially causing false-positive rejections of valid plans. Verify whether the scout-candidate removal path `remove_scout_candidate()` is always called before the plan is written so a stale candidate from a prior invocation cannot survive when the current run produces no scout. In `scripts/launch-claude-drafter.sh` and `launch-codex-drafter.sh`, the `filter_failed` branch removes `$DESIGN_CANON/scout-plan-manifest.json` — confirm this removal is correct when a prior successful run had written that file and the current run produces a malformed scout. Check that `$scout_candidate` and `$scout_filtered` temp files are always cleaned up on all exit paths (success, parse failure, exec failure). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: required-flag-propagation
archetypes.rationale: All three implementer launchers now treat --scout-manifest-path as a required flag; any caller that omits it will fail with exit 2 before spawning the coder, which would silently break the implement flow.
archetypes.prompt_body: Locate `skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh` (the only authorized caller per the doc) and verify it passes `--scout-manifest-path` to both `launch-codex-implement.sh` and `launch-cursor-implement.sh`. Verify the Claude implementer path (if dispatched through a different launcher) also receives the new argument or is exempt. Check that all early-exit paths in the launchers (token-budget cap, model-args preflight failure, auth preflight failure) emit `SCOUT_MANIFEST_WRITTEN=false` to maintain the `KEY=VALUE` stdout contract — the diff shows some paths were updated but verify consistency across all early returns. Confirm that the test harnesses for `test-codex-implementer` and `test-cursor-implementer` cover the new required flag in their flag-validation sections. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: emergency-merge-security
archetypes.rationale: SECURITY.md now documents --emergency and --merge as compatible; this is a reversal of the prior mutual-exclusion posture and warrants an independent read of the trust-boundary implications.
archetypes.prompt_body: The old SECURITY.md text stated `/implement --emergency` is 'mutually exclusive with `--merge` so a downgraded run cannot flow into automated merge paths'; the new text says they are 'compatible' with the same downgrade warnings. Verify whether `implement-preflight.sh` or any downstream script enforces any guard between `--emergency` and `--merge` that would prevent an untrusted plan body from being auto-merged. Check whether the `--emergency` bypass log and `Emergency: true` tracking metadata are preserved through the merge path so consumers of the merged PR can detect the downgrade. Assess whether the removal of the mutual-exclusion creates a scenario where a raw-issue-body-fallback plan (explicitly untrusted) could be implemented and merged without operator review of the trust downgrade. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
